name: Nigeria
summary: Africa's most populous country and a leading oil producer, undergoing painful reforms — fuel-subsidy removal and currency unification — under President Tinubu. Jihadist insurgency in the north-east and banditry in the north-west remain major threats.
strategicInterests: Economic stabilisation and investment inflows
Defeat Boko Haram / ISWAP and curb banditry
Regional leadership of ECOWAS after the Sahel juntas' exit
Raise oil output and domestic refining (Dangote refinery)

government.notes: GDP figure reflects the 2025 statistical rebasing.

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: Largest proven reserves in Africa after Libya

resources.name: Demographics
resources.note: Population projected to exceed 350 million by 2050

name: South Africa
summary: Africa's most industrialised economy and a BRICS founder, governed since 2024 by a multi-party Government of National Unity. Pretoria's non-aligned stance and its ICJ genocide case against Israel have strained ties with Washington; it hosted the 2025 G20 summit.
strategicInterests: Voice for Africa in the G20 and BRICS
Protect trade access (AGOA) amid US tariffs
Fix electricity and logistics bottlenecks
Reform-driven growth under the unity government

capabilities: Only state to have built and voluntarily dismantled nuclear weapons

government.system: Unitary parliamentary republic with executive president
government.notes: ANC-led Government of National Unity with the Democratic Alliance and others.

name: Ethiopia
summary: Africa's second most populous country and seat of the African Union, landlocked since Eritrea's independence. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, inaugurated in 2025, has intensified its Nile dispute with Egypt, while insurgencies persist in Amhara and Oromia.
strategicInterests: Secure sovereign access to the Red Sea
Operate the GERD and expand power exports
Contain internal insurgencies and a fragile Tigray peace
IMF-backed economic reform after floating the birr in 2024

capabilities: One of the largest armies in Africa

government.notes: Prosperity Party dominant; general election planned for 2026. USD GDP omitted — distorted by the 2024 currency float.

resources.name: Ethiopian Airlines
resources.note: Africa's largest carrier and a strategic hub

name: DR Congo
summary: The world's dominant cobalt supplier and a leading copper producer, central to battery supply chains. In early 2025 the Rwanda-backed M23 rebels seized Goma and Bukavu; a US-brokered peace agreement with Rwanda followed in June 2025 alongside a minerals-for-security framework.
strategicInterests: Restore sovereignty in the eastern provinces
Leverage cobalt export quotas to lift prices
Attract Western mining investment to balance Chinese dominance
Protect the Congo Basin rainforest and its carbon value

capabilities: Burundian troop support; UN MONUSCO mission

resources.name: Coltan, lithium & gold
resources.note: Manono lithium deposit among the world's largest

resources.name: Inga Falls
resources.note: Potentially the largest hydropower site on earth

name: Rwanda
summary: A small, tightly governed state with a highly capable military and an outsized regional role. UN experts report that Rwanda backs the M23 rebellion in eastern DR Congo, which Kigali frames as a response to threats from the FDLR militia.
strategicInterests: Neutralise the FDLR in eastern DR Congo
Economic and security influence in the Great Lakes
Peacekeeping and bilateral deployments (Mozambique, CAR)
Position Kigali as a services and conference hub

government.notes: Kagame has led the country since 2000.

resources.name: 3T minerals
resources.note: UN experts link part of Rwanda's exports to minerals smuggled from eastern DRC; Kigali denies this

name: Kenya
summary: East Africa's economic and diplomatic hub and a US Major Non-NATO Ally since 2024. Kenya leads the multinational security mission in Haiti, while youth-led protests over taxes and debt have challenged the government.
strategicInterests: Regional trade and logistics hub (Mombasa, LAPSSET corridor)
Security against al-Shabaab and stability in Somalia
Debt sustainability and investor confidence
Green energy leadership (geothermal)

resources.name: Port of Mombasa
resources.note: Gateway for Uganda, Rwanda, South Sudan and eastern DRC

name: Sudan
summary: Engulfed since April 2023 in a civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces, producing the world's largest displacement crisis and famine. The RSF captured El Fasher in October 2025, consolidating its hold on Darfur.
strategicInterests: SAF: defeat the RSF and preserve state authority
Access to external arms (Egypt, Turkey, Iran and others)
Humanitarian access and famine relief
Control of gold revenues and the Red Sea coast

government.notes: The RSF has declared a rival administration in areas it controls.

resources.name: Gold
resources.note: Main export; financing both warring sides

resources.name: Red Sea coast
resources.note: Port Sudan; Russian naval base agreement unratified
